mainTopic: רב פפא's smaller-than-promised field, brothers dividing an estate by lottery, and a third brother who returns after the division (רב vs. שמואל)
overview: This amud starts by finishing the story of רב פפא, who bought a field that the seller called 'twenty גריוי' but that measured only fifteen. אביי rules that רב פפא knew the field and accepted it as it was. He answers רב פפא's two challenges: the משנה about a shortfall of a sixth covers only a buyer who did not know the field, and the seller's 'twenty' meant 'as good as twenty'. Next comes a ברייתא of רבי יוסי: when brothers divide an estate by lottery, all of them acquire once the first lot is drawn. רבי אלעזר learns this from the dividing of ארץ ישראל by lottery. When that comparison is challenged, רב אשי explains instead that the brothers' agreement with each other makes the lottery work. Then רב and שמואל argue about two brothers who divided an estate before a third brother came back from overseas. רב cancels the division and שמואל keeps it, with each brother giving up a share. The גמרא defends רב against רבא's challenge about three partners. It then raises a challenge against שמואל from the case of selling a כור of grain, and this challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The field measured smaller, and אביי says the buyer accepted it
steps.stepSummary: The seller told רב פפא the field was twenty גריוי. It measured only fifteen. אביי ruled: 'You knew it and you accepted it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The seller said to him: 'It is twenty גריוי.' רב פפא measured it, and it was only fifteen. He came before אביי, and אביי said to him: 'You knew the field and you accepted it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story about רב פפא buying a field. The field turned out smaller than the seller said, and אביי rules that the sale stands as it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fifteen out of twenty is a quarter short, so you would expect the buyer to have a complaint. אביי says no: רב פפא knew this field, so he really bought what he saw, whatever the number. The next steps test this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of land: the area planted with one גריו (a סאה) of seed
He measured it
You knew it and you accepted it

phrases.english: He said to him: It is twenty griv.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the seller, speaking to רב פפא, who is buying the field. The story starts just before this line.

phrases.english: He measured it, and it was only fifteen.
He came before Abaye,
He said to him: You knew and you accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the case of רב פפא's purchase, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer who knew the field he bought cannot complain that it is smaller than the number the seller gave.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about a shortfall of a sixth
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects: the משנה teaches that if the shortfall reaches a sixth, the seller must give back money. Here it is short by even more than that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: if the difference is less than a sixth, the field is his. If it reaches a sixth, the seller must take off the difference.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks אביי's ruling using a משנה. The משנה says a big enough shortfall must be paid back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts the limit at a sixth: a smaller gap is forgiven, but a gap of a sixth must be repaid. Here five out of twenty is missing, a quarter, which is more than a sixth. So it looks like the seller should have to pay back the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? A formula that opens a challenge
One sixth
It has reached him: it is his, with no adjustment
He must deduct, meaning take it off the price

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the mishna:
Less than one-sixth – it is his,
phrases.notes: He means: if the field is short by less than a sixth, the buyer just keeps it.

phrases.english: Up to one-sixth – he must deduct!

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that רב פפא has no claim
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires repayment when the shortfall reaches a sixth. Here it is a quarter, so the seller should have to pay.

steps.title: The משנה is about a buyer who did not know the field
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers: the משנה is about a buyer who did not know the field. A buyer who knew it accepted it as it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule applies where the buyer is not familiar with the field. But where he is familiar with it, he knew it and accepted it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי limits the משנה to a buyer who did not know the land. רב פפא did know it, so the משנה does not apply to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule about a sixth protects a buyer who relied on the numbers. A buyer who already knew the field was buying the field itself and not the number, so the shortfall does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: These words: this rule applies only...
He is familiar with it, he knows the field

phrases.english: These words apply
where he is not familiar with it,
but where he is familiar with it –
he knew and accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא קִים לֵיהּ בְּגַוַּהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the משנה covers only a buyer who did not know the field
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule about a sixth applies to every buyer.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule protects only a buyer who did not know the field. A buyer who knew it accepted it as it is.

steps.title: But the seller said 'twenty'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא pushes back again: even if I knew the field, the seller clearly told me it was twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a second objection. The seller gave a specific number, so how can that number not count?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the field is one thing, but the seller made a clear statement of size. רב פפא argues that the stated number should bind the seller, and since it was wrong, the sale should be adjusted.

keyTerms.meaning: But look... A word that opens an objection
Twenty

phrases.english: But he said 'twenty' to me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge after the answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a buyer who knew the field accepted it as it is
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seller's clear statement of 'twenty' should count no matter what the buyer knew.

steps.title: 'Twenty' meant 'as good as twenty'
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the seller meant the field is as good and as productive as a field of twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: He meant that it is as good as twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי reads the seller's words differently: 'twenty' was praise of the field's quality and not a measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב פפא knew the real size, the seller's 'twenty' could not have been a promise about size. It was a way of saying the field yields as much as a twenty-unit field, so it was not a false claim.

keyTerms.meaning: That it is good, that it is worth as much

steps.whatToRemember: A buyer who knew the field cannot claim a shortfall. Even the seller's number is understood as praise of the field's quality and not as a measurement.

phrases.english: He said to him: That it is as good as twenty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 and closes the story.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Twenty' was a promise about the field's size.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Twenty' described the field's quality, so the seller made no false claim.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: brothers acquire once the first lot is drawn
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: when brothers divide their inheritance by lottery, as soon as one lot comes up, all of them acquire their shares.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יוסי says: brothers who divided an estate, once the lot came up for one of them, all of them acquired.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about brothers dividing an estate by drawing lots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that a lottery itself finalizes the split. After the first brother's lot is drawn, nobody can back out, and every share, including the ones not yet drawn, is acquired.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Brothers who divided (an inheritance)
A lot, a lottery
They acquired

steps.confusionAlert: It is not only the brother whose lot came up who acquires. Once one lot is drawn, all the brothers acquire their shares.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
Brothers who divided,
once the lot came up for one of them –
they all acquired.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: הָאַחִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: acquiring through a lottery.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When brothers divide by lottery, once one lot is drawn, all of them acquire their shares.

steps.title: Why does a lottery acquire?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is for רבי יוסי's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a lottery should work to acquire. This question sets up רבי אלעזר's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lottery is not one of the usual ways of acquiring, like paying money or doing an act of taking possession. So the rule needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for a lottery working as a way to acquire

steps.title: Learned from the first dividing of ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר: just as ארץ ישראל was first divided among the tribes by lottery, brothers too can divide by lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is like the first dividing of ארץ ישראל. Just as the first dividing was by lottery, here too it is by lottery.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the source: the land was first divided among the tribes by lottery, and that is the model for brothers dividing an inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תורה's own dividing of the land used a lottery, a lottery is a valid way to split shared property. That is why the brothers' lottery finalizes the division.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the first (dividing of) ארץ ישראל
Just as... so too here: a formula for comparing two cases

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's first answer: the brothers' lottery is modeled on the dividing of ארץ ישראל by lottery. Step 9 challenges this source, and in step 10 רב אשי gives a different reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a lottery can be a real way of acquiring when partners or heirs divide property.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Like the beginning of Eretz Yisrael –
phrases.notes: He means the very first time the land was split up among the tribes.

phrases.english: just as the beginning was by lot,
so too here, by lot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כִּתְחִלַּת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A lottery works because the first dividing of ארץ ישראל was done by lottery.

steps.title: Must brothers also use a lottery box and the אורים ותומים?
steps.stepSummary: If the brothers' lottery is learned from the division of ארץ ישראל, then it should also need a lottery box and the אורים ותומים, just as that division did.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you compare the two: just as there the land was divided with a lottery box and the אורים ותומים, here too the brothers should need a lottery box and the אורים ותומים?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's comparison by taking it further. If brothers learn from the tribes, they should need everything the tribes used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר learned the lottery from the way ארץ ישראל was divided. But that division also used a קלפי and the אורים ותומים. The challenge is that you cannot copy only one part of the model and drop the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: A box or container that the lots were drawn from
The holy breastplate of the כהן גדול, used to get answers from Heaven
"Just as there... so too here", a way of comparing two cases

phrases.english: If so, just as there
phrases.notes: "There" is the first division of ארץ ישראל among the tribes, from step 8.

phrases.english: it was done with a lottery box and the אורים ותומים,
so too here, should it need a lottery box and the אורים ותומים?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי – מַה לְּהַלָּן בְּקַלְפִּי וְאוּרִים וְתוּמִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's source from step 8 by pushing the comparison further.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's comparison of the brothers' lottery to the division of ארץ ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison works, it should bring along all the features of the original division, including the קלפי and the אורים ותומים, which brothers obviously do not use.

steps.title: רב אשי: the lottery works because the brothers agree
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the lottery works because the brothers are happy to agree with each other, and so they fully transfer the shares to one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: because of the satisfaction they get from going along with each other, they fully commit and transfer ownership to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. He gives a new reason the lottery works, based on the brothers' agreement and not on the tribes' model.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The acquisition does not come from copying how ארץ ישראל was divided, so no קלפי or אורים ותומים is needed. It comes from the brothers' own good will. Each one is pleased that the others accept the lottery, and that pleasure is enough for them to fully commit and give each other ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefit or satisfaction
They listen to and go along with each other
They fully commit and transfer ownership

steps.whatToRemember: The lottery between brothers works because of their mutual agreement and satisfaction. Nothing like the קלפי or אורים ותומים is needed.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
With that satisfaction
that they listen to each other,
they fully commit and transfer ownership to each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by giving a new reason for the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source with a reason based on the brothers' agreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lottery works only because it copies the division of ארץ ישראל, so it would need all of that division's features.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lottery works because the brothers agree and are pleased with each other, so no special tools are needed.

steps.title: A brother comes back from overseas after the division
steps.stepSummary: Two brothers divided the estate, and then a third brother arrived from overseas. רב says the division is cancelled. שמואל says each brother takes off a share for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: two brothers divided the estate, and then a brother came to them from overseas. רב said: the division is cancelled. שמואל said: they each take off a portion for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רב and שמואל argue about what happens when the brothers divided without knowing about a third brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the whole first division is void and they must divide again three ways. According to שמואל, the first division stays, and each of the two brothers simply gives part of his share to the newcomer.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was stated", which introduces an argument between אמוראים
A country overseas, meaning far away
The division is cancelled
They each take off a portion for the third brother

phrases.english: It was stated: two brothers who divided the estate,
and a brother came to them from overseas;
רב said: the division is cancelled,
and שמואל said: they each take off a portion.
phrases.notes: The word comes from "a handful": each brother hands over a bit of his part, and the division stays as it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related discussion about brothers dividing an estate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the original division is void. שמואל: the division stands, and each brother gives part of his share to the third brother.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב with three partners
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן: if רב cancels the division, he should also cancel it when two of three partners divided on their own. But that seems wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: according to רב, who says the division is cancelled, it seems the judgment goes back. If so, take three partners, and two of them went and divided. Would the division be cancelled here too?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב's view. He compares it to a case of three partners where two of them divided without the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא understands רב to mean that a division with a mistake is completely undone. If that is true, then when two of three partners divide without the third, it should also be undone. The question shows the problem with such a broad rule.

keyTerms.meaning: "So it seems", which draws a conclusion
The judgment goes back and is reopened
"But if so", which shows a problem that follows from the idea
Three people, here meaning three partners

phrases.english: רבא said to רב נחמן:
According to רב, who said the division is cancelled,
it seems that the judgment goes back;
phrases.notes: He means that a division done by mistake is undone completely.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, הָנֵי בֵּי תְלָתָא דְּקָיְימִי,
phrases.english: but if so, take these three partners who stand together,
and two of them went and divided,
would the division also be cancelled?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: לְרַב דְּאָמַר בָּטְלָה מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the division is cancelled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a mistaken division is fully undone, then two of three partners dividing without the third should also be undone. That seems not to be the case.

steps.title: The difference: did they know there were three?
steps.stepSummary: The partners knew from the start that there were three of them. The brothers thought there were only two, so their whole division was built on a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them?! There, they went in from the start knowing there were three. Here, they did not go in from the start knowing there were three.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer rejects רבא's comparison. It shows that the two cases are basically different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The partners knew all along that there were three of them, so their division was planned with three in mind. The brothers divided as if there were only two, so the whole basis of their division was wrong. That is why רב cancels it.

keyTerms.meaning: "How can you compare?!", which rejects a comparison
They went in with this understanding
From the beginning

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, the division is cancelled only because the brothers divided thinking there were two of them. When everyone knew from the start that there were three, the case is different.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, נְחִיתוּ אַדַּעְתָּא דְּבֵי תְּלָתָא מֵעִיקָּרָא;
phrases.english: There, they went in from the start knowing there were three;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, לָא נְחִיתוּ אַדַּעְתָּא דְּבֵי תְלָתָא מֵעִיקָּרָא.
phrases.english: here, they did not go in from the start knowing there were three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 12 by showing how the two cases differ.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's rule means every mistaken division is undone, including two of three partners dividing.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב cancels the division only when it was based on a wrong idea of how many heirs there were, not when everyone knew there were three.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges שמואל from the case of selling a כור of grain
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: if שמואל keeps the brothers' division in place, does he hold that a flawed deal still stands? But רב and שמואל both say a sale made as one whole unit can be cancelled even at the last סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: According to שמואל, who says each brother gives up a share, does that mean the original division stands? But רב and שמואל both say: if a seller says 'I am selling you a כור for thirty,' he can back out even at the last סאה. If he says 'a כור for thirty, a סאה for a סלע,' then the buyer acquires each סאה as it is measured out!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks שמואל's ruling from step 11. He brings a ruling that שמואל himself agrees to, which seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a deal is made as one whole package (a כור for thirty), nothing is finished until the whole package is done, so the seller can cancel all of it. The brothers' division was also one package built on there being two heirs. So once that package fails, the whole division should fall apart, like רב says, and not stay in place with small cuts, like שמואל says.

keyTerms.meaning: They take off a little: each brother gives up a share from his portion for the third brother
The original ruling or division stands
A large measure of grain, equal to thirty סאה
A smaller measure of grain; thirty make a כור
A coin
To back out of a deal

steps.confusionAlert: The two sale cases are the same amount of grain at the same price. The only difference is the wording. 'A כור for thirty' makes it one whole deal. Adding 'a סאה for a סלע' makes it many small deals, so each סאה is acquired as it is measured out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key question for שמואל: why is the brothers' division not treated like one whole deal that falls apart completely?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
According to Shmuel, who says they take off a share,
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's ruling from step 11: each of the two brothers gives up some of his share for the third brother.

phrases.english: is that to say the original ruling stands?!
But don't Rav and Shmuel both say:
'I am selling you a kor for thirty',
he can back out of it
even at the last se'a.
'A kor for thirty, a se'a for a sela,
I am selling you',
he acquires each one, one by one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: לִשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמַר מְקַמְּצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the גמרא defended רב in steps 12-13, it now challenges שמואל's side of the same argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the brothers' division stays in place and each brother just gives up a share (מקמצין).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל agrees that a sale made as one whole unit is completely cancelled, even after most of the grain was handed over. The brothers' division was one whole unit built on the mistaken idea that there were only two heirs. So it should be completely cancelled too, not kept with small changes.
